question.prompt:
The area of each of the four congruent L-shaped regions of this \(100\)-inch by \(100\)-inch square is \(\dfrac{3}{16}\) of the total area. How many inches long is the side of the center square?

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The four L-shaped regions and the center square fill the large square without overlapping, so subtracting the L-shaped areas gives the center's area.

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

Together, the four L-shaped regions occupy
\[
4\cdot\frac{3}{16}=\frac{12}{16}=\frac34
\]
of the total area. The center therefore occupies \(1-\frac34=\frac14\) of it. Since the large square has area \(100\cdot100=10{,}000\) square inches, the center has area
\[
\frac14\cdot10{,}000=2500\text{ square inches}.
\]
A square's area is its side length multiplied by itself. Because \(50\cdot50=2500\) and a side length is positive, the center's side is \(\boxed{50\text{ inches}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Find the area left for the center
